ABOUT THIS EXPERIMENT

What does the neural circuit do?

Road and obstacle signals are encoded as stimuli for a MaleCNS visual circuit. Spikes propagated through real connections are read out as steering and braking. The sensory encoder and output mapping are engineered; the fly has not learned to drive.

This connectome-inspired experiment uses simplified LIF neurons. It is not a complete biophysical fly model or evidence that a biological fly can drive.
